children: Sreeradha Basu & Brinda Sarkar Bengaluru: Corporate offsites and incentive trips are gathering pace again after a subdued first half of the year, when geopolitical tensions forced many companies to put travel on hold. Businesses are now rescheduling deferred trips and signing off on fresh programmes, with destinations ranging from Goa and Jaipur to Thailand and Japan. From luxury villas and local experiences to sporting events and gala dinners, companies are looking to pack more into the time teams spend together.

Travel firms are reporting a gradual recovery, driven by an increase in leadership retreats, incentive travel and large-scale employee engagement programmes. "Corporate offsites and incentive travel are entering a recovery phase. We are seeing deferred groups being rescheduled and executed alongside fresh bookings for coming months, indicating a gradual return in activity," said Rajeev Kale, president and country head - holidays, MICE and visa at Thomas Cook (India). Goa and Dehradun are among the popular domestic choices, while international interest spans Japan, South Africa, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, as well as Australia and New Zealand, said Kale. Demand ranges from large-scale programmes for entire teams, with varying budget and accommodation standards, to exclusive, premium experiences for top performers. Planning is becoming more elaborate, particularly for larger groups.

title: Team Trips are Back on Corp Calendars
